reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of relative advantage stems from the statistical duality between absolute and relative performance measures. In noisy settings, absolute scores are contaminated by shared environmental factors η, which affect both competitors equally. The difference R = (XA − XB) cancels these common terms, leaving only the true difference (μA − μB) plus residual noise. This is formalized in Theorem 2.3, which states that R ~ N(μA − μB, σA² + σB²). The key operational principle is that when η dominates individual variability (ση >> σ_indiv), relative performance becomes more informative than absolute. This is quantified by the SNR diagnostic ση/σ_indiv. When this ratio exceeds a critical value, the relative measure provides superior discrimination power, as shown in Theorem 2.6. The equivalence between explicit relativization and implicit learning in linear models (via weights wA = 1, wB = -1) confirms that relativization is not just heuristic but mathematically optimal under certain conditions. This principle underpins GSI’s Bayesian inference and GSE’s state transition modeling, where environmental noise must be canceled to extract meaningful signals.
